ledger.claim: POL-NS-01 is conjunctive, and limb (d) requires that the trip was terminated by the DRIVER with a recognised reason code. The only thing in this bundle that says the driver terminated the trip is a single telemetry field (trip_record.cancelled_by = DRIVER with cancellation_reason_code RIDER_NO_SHOW): both parties' own accounts record the RIDER as the cancelling party - the rider states 'I waited and cancelled' and the driver's own statement says 'she didn't answer, she cancelled'. Limb (d) is therefore not affirmatively carried on the face of the record, and where a limb of POL-NS-01 fails the baseline charge is not made out at all. At minimum the unresolved question of who terminated the trip should not be resolved against the rider, who is the party being charged.

Even taking the driver's case at its highest, his qualifying dwell clears the STANDARD minimum by only 50 seconds - 350 seconds against the 300 second floor (derived.arrival.longest_qualifying_run.duration_sec 350.0, shortfall_sec -50.0) - and it is a single run: run_count is 1, the excursions list is empty, and POL-NS-06(i)'s limb is unavailable. Nothing in the record may be used to supplement or bridge that run, because the traffic advisory artifact EV-ADVIS-00624-01 is MISSING (weight 0.0, issue MISSING_ARTIFACT, 'No advisory covers the pickup road in this window'), so no kerb restriction, enforcement, closure or accident can be invoked to add time. The rider asks the judge to hold the chargeable dwell strictly to the computed run and to no more than the computed run.

The rider does NOT rely on POL-NS-04 and I say so plainly rather than stretch it. Limb (a) requires a locating or coordinating message from the rider in the chat log, and the chat export for this trip is empty - 0 messages, 0 first/last message timestamps, consistent with trip_record.chat_message_count of 0 - so no such message exists. Limb (c) requires the rider's device within the 100 m STANDARD presence radius for the majority of qualifying fixes, and the rider track records 0 qualifying fixes inside that radius (rider minimum distance 689.68 m, maximum 699.35 m). Both limbs fail on this record and that clause cannot exonerate the rider. Nothing else in the bundle is impaired either: clock skew between the arrival marker and the nearest fix is 2 seconds, the trace has no gaps (max_gap_sec 0.0), and the SGD 4.00 charged equals the greater of the STANDARD zone fee and the RYDE_X tier fee, so the rider does not seek PARTIAL_REFUND on integrity grounds.

The only profile counter that could engage the escalation limb for possible rider abuse is rider_profile.no_show_disputes_30d, and it stands at 2, below the 3-dispute threshold POL-NS-09(d) sets. No abuse limb is engaged against the rider on this record.

ledger.claim: The trip record carries a driver 'arrived' event at 2026-09-24T12:45:52 and shows the trip terminated by the driver at 12:51:50 under cancellation_reason_code RIDER_NO_SHOW — one of the three codes POL-NS-01(d) recognises — with no boarding event and no started_at. POL-NS-01 limbs (a) and (d) are satisfied on the face of the record, so the anchor clause is live and the cancellation fee is chargeable unless something in POL-NS-03 to POL-NS-06 displaces it.

The GPS trace puts the driver inside the 50 m STANDARD arrival radius two seconds BEFORE the recorded arrival event: the longest qualifying in-geofence run begins at 12:45:50 against an arrived_at of 12:45:52, carries 36 consecutive qualifying fixes, and the driver's minimum distance to the pin across the whole track is 5.8 m. POL-NS-01 limb (b) and the POL-NS-02 geofence test are both satisfied, and no low-accuracy filtering question arises because every fix in the trace is admissible at weight 1.0.

The driver's continuous qualifying dwell inside the geofence runs 350 seconds, from 12:45:50 to 12:51:40, measured from the first qualifying in-geofence fix and not from the 'arrived' tap. The minimum for a STANDARD pickup zone class is 300 seconds. The driver therefore held position 50 seconds beyond the required dwell, and POL-NS-01 limb (c) is satisfied with a margin.

POL-NS-06 has nothing to operate on: the measured dwell exceeds the minimum, so the shortfall is negative (shortfall_sec = -50.0 seconds) rather than positive. There is no premature cancellation, no waiting-period defect, and consequently no route to a refund of the cancellation-fee line on a shortfall basis.

POL-NS-05 does not touch this arrival. The clause bites only where the arrival marker places the driver more than 300 m from the pin or travelling at 15 km/h or above. At the marker the driver was stationary — his track's distinct speeds include 0.0 km/h and his minimum distance to the pin is 5.8 m — so the marker is true, not false, and the waiting clock needs no recomputation under this clause.

POL-NS-03 is not engaged either. That clause governs a driver stationary OUTSIDE the POL-NS-02 arrival radius but within 400 m of the pin — the wrong-face-of-the-building case. The driver's stationary fixes sit 5.8 m from the pickup pin, inside the 50 m STANDARD arrival radius, so this is an on-pin arrival and the wrong-entrance fault allocation (including the pin-ambiguity goodwill route) never opens.

POL-NS-04 cannot exonerate the rider. Limb (a) requires a locating or coordinating rider message in the chat log, and the chat log for this trip is empty — message_count 0, no first or last message timestamp, no messages at all — so the predicate of the clause is simply absent. Limb (b) fails independently: the record shows the driver placed two in-app calls, at 12:46:40 (20 s) and 12:49:40 (25 s), both unanswered, and a recorded call by the driver defeats the clause regardless of what the chat shows.

The rider's own telemetry contradicts her assertion that she waited at the pickup point. Her device fixes sit roughly 690 m from the pin (minimum 689.68 m, mean 694.44 m) and none of her 42 fixes qualifies inside the 100 m STANDARD rider-presence radius (rider_qualifying_fix_count 0). Her claim of a no-show by the driver is therefore not a claim of a driver who failed to turn up, but of a rider whose own device was not at the pin.

The traffic advisory is MISSING (EV-ADVIS-00624-01, status MISSING, weight 0.0, issue code MISSING_ARTIFACT) and its absence is itself citable. POL-NS-06(i) permits separate in-geofence intervals to be summed only where a present and populated advisory of type KERB_RESTRICTION, ENFORCEMENT, CLOSURE or ACCIDENT covers the pickup road; no advisory covers this road in this window, so that route is closed — and in any event the trace shows a single in-geofence run (run_count 1), so there is no second interval to sum.

The fee line is internally consistent, so there is no POL-NS-08(d) fare defect. The resolution rule takes the GREATER of the zone-class fee and the vehicle-tier fee: STANDARD zone class is SGD 4.00 and the RYDE_X vehicle tier is SGD 4.00, giving SGD 4.00, which is exactly the cancellation_fee itemised in the ledger and the fee_charged figure the ledger derives. The ledger needs no correction.

The driver is owed money under POL-NS-07. Eighty percent of the SGD 4.00 cancellation fee is SGD 3.20, which the ledger itself computes as driver_compensation. The anti-farming guard does not trip: no_show_terminations_30d is 1, below the absolute threshold of 4, and 1 divided by completed_trips_30d of 118 is 0.008, far below the 0.08 rate threshold. Both limbs are required and neither holds, so compensation is payable and is not withheld.

No POL-NS-09 escalation trigger is open, and POL-GEN-02 sets a confidence cap this record comfortably clears. Every artifact cited carries weight_multiplier 1.0; the only sub-1.0 artifact is the MISSING advisory at 0.0, which carries no fact the ruling rests on. There is no clock skew (arrival marker 12:45:52 against nearest fix 12:45:50, a 2 second difference, well inside the 90 second limit), no sampling gap (max_gap_sec 0.0 across 67 fixes at a 10 s cadence), and no chat defect (0 messages recorded, 0 asserted). The counterparty dispute counters are 0 for both parties, the driver's no-show terminations are 1, and the rider's no_show_disputes_30d of 2 sits below the trigger of 3.

The disposition follows from all of the above: the rider's claim is not supported, so the present payment state stands — payment_status CHARGED and refund_issued_sgd 0.00 are left undisturbed under POL-GEN-03, which is what the rider's request for the fee back cannot survive. The outcome the case produces is DRIVER_COMPENSATION of SGD 3.20, with amount_sgd mirroring driver_compensation_sgd as POL-GEN-03 requires on that ruling value.

ruling.explanation:
To the rider: the SGD 4.00 no-show fee stands, no part of it is refunded, and the driver is paid SGD 3.20 in compensation. POL-NS-01 needs four conditions for the fee to be chargeable and all four hold on this record. (a) The trip record carries a driver 'arrived' event at 12:45:52, with no boarding event and no started_at. (b) The GPS trace places the driver inside the 50 m STANDARD arrival radius at and before that moment: a 36-fix qualifying run begins 12:45:50 and his closest approach to your pin is 5.8 m. (c) His continuous stop inside the geofence ran 350 seconds, from 12:45:50 to 12:51:40, measured from the first qualifying in-geofence fix and not from the tap, against the 300-second STANDARD minimum, so he held position 50 seconds beyond the required dwell. (d) The trip record shows the trip terminated by the driver at 12:51:50, after the dwell was complete, with reason code RIDER_NO_SHOW and no boarding event.

Your account that 'he never came' is contradicted by the GPS trace, and your own device telemetry does not support your statement that you waited: your fixes sit about 690 m from the pin throughout (minimum 689.68 m), and none of your 42 fixes qualifies inside the 100 m STANDARD rider-presence radius. Your further argument that limb (d) fails because you and the driver both say you cancelled is rejected: POL-NS-01(d)'s test is the trip record, and the trip record is the platform's own and records cancelled_by = DRIVER with reason RIDER_NO_SHOW. An account does not decide a limb a clause assigns to the platform record, and this is not a contradiction of the kind POL-NS-09(b) names (arrival, dwell or rider presence) — and on those three points the GPS and the record agree.

The remaining displacing routes do not apply. POL-NS-03 (wrong entrance) needs the driver stationary outside the arrival radius; he was 5.8 m from the pin. POL-NS-04 requires a locating message from you — the chat log is empty (0 messages) — and the driver placed two in-app calls (12:46:40, 20 s; 12:49:40, 25 s), both unanswered, which defeats the clause independently; your POL-NS-04 concession is accepted. POL-NS-05 does not bite: at the arrival marker the driver was stationary (0.0 km/h in his track) and 5.8 m from the pin, so the marker is true. POL-NS-06 does not bite: the dwell exceeds the minimum, leaving a shortfall of -50 seconds. The MISSING traffic advisory (EV-ADVIS-00624-01, weight 0.0, MISSING_ARTIFACT) carries no fact and is not relied on; the single in-geofence run would in any event leave nothing to accumulate.

To the driver: your compensation is payable. POL-NS-01 is satisfied in full, no clause from POL-NS-03 to POL-NS-06 displaces it, and POL-NS-07 pays 80 percent of the SGD 4.00 cancellation fee itemised in the fare breakdown, which is SGD 3.20, the residual SGD 0.80 being the platform service fee. The anti-farming guard does not trip: no_show_terminations_30d is 1 (below the absolute threshold of 4) and its ratio to 118 completed 30-day trips is about 0.008 (below 0.08); both limbs must hold to withhold compensation and neither does. The rider's request for the fee back is not supported, so the present state stands (payment_status CHARGED, refund_issued_sgd 0.00); because compensation is paid, the ruling value is DRIVER_COMPENSATION and amount_sgd mirrors driver_compensation_sgd.

Your remark that the rider 'disputes everything to get vouchers' carries no adverse finding against her: prior_disputes_filed (14), prior_disputes_upheld (9) and prior_no_show_flags (6) are context-only under POL-GEN-01 and may not establish anything about this trip, and the only citable abuse counter, rider_profile.no_show_disputes_30d, is 2, below the POL-NS-09(d) threshold of 3. No escalation trigger is open: confidence is above the 0.70 floor, the parties share no trailing-90-day disputes, the anti-farming check does not trip, and no deciding fact rests on an impaired artifact — the arrival, dwell, termination and fee facts are each carried by weight-1.0 artifacts (GPS trace, trip record, fare breakdown). No clause produces a referral.

The judge was asked 4 times on the same inputs and every draft agreed on this ruling, so it is carried unanimously (vote agreement 1.00).
